display.title: Key idea Key idea
display.body: The energy a plant grows on is captured from light, not taken in from the soil. The energy a plant grows on is captured from light, not taken in from the soil.

display.text: The green parts of a plant — mostly its leaves — absorb **light energy**. The leaf uses that energy to make the plant's own **food**: a sugar built from water drawn up out of the soil and carbon dioxide taken in from the air. The green parts of a plant — mostly its leaves — absorb **light energy**. The leaf uses that energy to make the plant's own **food**: a sugar built from water drawn up out of the soil and carbon dioxide taken in from the air.

outputs: sugar (the plant's food) sugar (the plant's food)

display.text: The energy stored inside that sugar is what the plant spends on building new leaves, stem and roots. The energy stored inside that sugar is what the plant spends on building new leaves, stem and roots.
Follow the energy, step by step Follow the energy, step by step

items: Sunlight reaches the leaf. Sunlight reaches the leaf.
The leaf's green parts capture that light energy. The leaf's green parts capture that light energy.

The captured energy is used to build sugar from water and carbon dioxide. The energy is now stored inside food the plant has made for itself. The captured energy is used to build sugar from water and carbon dioxide. The energy is now stored inside food the plant has made for itself.

The plant breaks some of that sugar down again and uses the released energy to build new leaves, stem and roots. That is growth. The plant breaks some of that sugar down again and uses the released energy to build new leaves, stem and roots. That is growth.

display.text: So what is the soil for? So what is the soil for?
